guide.headline: USC's front and third downs are strangling Washington
guide.hook: A top-2-percent passer has gone quiet while two trench mismatches decide whether Washington can ever get untracked.

items.title: Maiava's clean efficiency vs his rough day
items.what: Jayden Maiava came in averaging 9.5 yards per attempt with 14 touchdowns against two interceptions, numbers that put him in the top 2 percent of FBS quarterbacks this season. So far today he is 12 of 19 for just 143 yards with one interception and zero touchdowns, a sharp drop from his season line. If he starts resetting his feet and hitting throws outside the numbers like his tape suggests he can, USC's offense should open back up.
items.when: Watch his next two or three dropbacks after the interception

items.title: USC owns third and long
items.what: USC ranks No. 3 of 138 nationally on passing downs, converting 47 percent of the time, while Washington's defense sits at No. 57 on passing downs, stopping only 27 percent. That is a 40 percentile point gap, the kind that breaks a defense's game plan over four quarters. Two third-and-long conversions for USC in a half is the sign Washington's pressure plan is already failing.
items.when: Every third-and-8 or longer USC faces
items.who: USC on passing downs vs Washington pressure

items.title: USC's front is winning the line
items.what: USC's defensive front ranks No. 39 of 138 at the line of scrimmage at 2.59, while Washington's offensive line ranks No. 106 in line yards per carry at 2.82. That is a 49 percentile point gap in USC's favor up front. Tackles for loss piling up early is the clearest sign Washington's run game never gets to the second level today.
items.when: On Washington's first-down runs, especially in the first quarter

guide.cardLine: Watch whether USC's 40-point passing-downs edge and 49-point front edge finally bury Washington, or if Maiava's quiet day keeps this one close.
